source.title: Effective Elastic Scaling of Deep Learning Workloads
source.authors: Vaibhav Saxena; K. Jayaram; Saurav Basu; Y. Sabharwal; Ashish Verma

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether changing batch size during training can preserve final accuracy, a different measure relevant to V5’s claim that adapting the recipe can reduce large-batch penalties.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a VGG11/CIFAR100 batch-size experiment. Other optimizer and scheduling results concern workload throughput or job completion, not generalization. Cited prior work is not recorded as a result.
record.test_reason: The scheduling method relies on accuracy being preserved within a permissible batch-size range. Its accuracy experiment compares dynamic schedules with fixed batch size 512 over 160 epochs, but establishes neither a large-versus-small batch penalty nor its removal by an adapted recipe. This does not directly test V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the supporting accuracy experiment. The paper's main conclusion is that optimizing GPU allocation and batch size within user-specified permissible ranges improves cluster throughput and job completion time.
record.recipe_differences: Tests dynamically varying batch size against fixed batch-size training and reports final accuracy; it does not test the large-batch generalization gap as framed in the original studies.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch-size variation pattern; the paper reports three patterns together but does not give their individual results.

fits_no_version.finding: VGG11 on CIFAR100 trained for 160 epochs with three dynamic batch-size patterns within 128–1024 reportedly finishes within ±0.5% accuracy of fixed batch size 512.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Changing batch size during training within a permissible range can preserve final accuracy relative to a fixed intermediate batch size.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE/ACM International Symposium on Modeling, Analysis, and Simulation On Computer and Telecommunication Systems
record.problems: The accuracy comparison is described as similar within ± 0.5%, but the text does not provide exact accuracy values, uncertainty methodology, or individual results for the three dynamic patterns. The experiment reports final accuracy, not a train-test generalization gap.
record.rows_left_out: No other results qualify as rows for the listed versions. The other experimental results measure job completions, throughput, scaling efficiency, job drops, or completion time.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label held-out generalization.
Width beyond zero training error and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and local connectivity.
Optimizer comparisons and tuning-dependent held-out performance.

Large-versus-small batch held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets, workload-dependent thresholds, and whether recipe adaptations remove an established penalty. The experiment does hold epochs fixed at 160.
Dropout and weight-decay effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Test-accuracy effects of removing memorized training examples.

record.verdict_notes: Figure 2's graphical values are unavailable in the supplied text. Scheduling throughput, completion times, and job-drop results do not measure generalization.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and generalization on natural labels.
Width beyond the interpolation threshold and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Does not compare large and small batches under a fixed epoch budget, or evaluate workload-dependent batch-size thresholds; tests dynamic batch-size changes against a fixed batch-size baseline.
Sharpness or other measured properties tracking the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: VGG11

rows.operation_detail: Trained with a fixed batch size throughout training.
rows.value: final accuracy reference for comparison; exact value not stated
rows.note: The text identifies the red fixed-BS curve but gives no numerical final accuracy for it.
rows.check: A fixed-batch accuracy reference alone cannot establish V5's batch-size effect. The exact accuracy and whether it is held-out accuracy are unspecified in the supplied text.

rows.subject: VGG11
rows.stage_stated: trained on the dataset CIFAR100 for 160 epochs
rows.operation_detail: Trained with batch size increased or decreased at random epochs within the stated range.
rows.measure: Final accuracy compared with fixed batch size of 512
rows.baseline: fixed batch size of 512 images throughout training
rows.note: The paper reports the three dynamic patterns together; individual curve values are not stated.
rows.check: Similar accuracy across dynamic schedules within a selected permissible range does not establish recovery from a large-batch penalty. The reported ±0.5% describes accuracy similarity; it is not identified as statistical uncertainty. Held-out evaluation is not specified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: VGG11 on CIFAR100, 160 epochs, dynamic batch size within 128-1024 images
reader_labels.reason: The authors report similar final accuracy (± 0.5%) for three dynamic batch-size patterns versus fixed batch size 512 (R2). This supports batch-size adaptation preserving accuracy in this setting.
